title: No driving
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in cardiology. Mr Kane, 46, had an implantable defibrillator fitted after a cardiac arrest. Earlier today the cardiologist explained that he must not drive for some months and must tell the DVLA.

When you see him, he is distressed. He drives a small delivery van, on an ordinary car licence, for a living, and asks, "How am I supposed to support my family?"
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Suggest he talks to his employer about other duties he could do for now.
options.brief: Practical help with his main worry.
options.detailed: His employer may be able to offer other work, and occupational health or a welfare adviser may help. It ranks third.

options.text: Tell him the rules for van drivers are often ignored.
options.detailed: This encourages him to break rules that protect him and the public. It ranks fourth only because it is less direct than the last option.

options.text: Suggest he keeps driving until he finds other work.
options.detailed: If he lost consciousness while driving, he could kill himself or others. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Check he understands that he mustn't drive and must tell the DVLA.
options.brief: The safety message must be understood, however hard it is.
options.detailed: He may not have taken in everything earlier. Making sure he understands the rules protects him and others. It ranks second because it comes better after acknowledging his distress.

options.text: Acknowledge how hard this is, and ask how it affects his family.
options.brief: He needs to feel heard before practical planning.
options.detailed: He has had life-changing news. Acknowledging his distress and asking about the impact helps him feel heard and shows you what support he needs. It ranks first.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond to a patient's distress about life-changing news, while keeping a safety message clear.
explanation.keyDetails: He must not drive. He drives for a living. He has already been told the rules. He is distressed about money.
explanation.reasoning: [E] responds to his distress, [D] checks the safety message, and [A] helps practically. [B] undermines the rules, and [C] actively encourages unsafe driving.
explanation.competing: Some would put the safety message first. He has already been told, so the key responds to his distress first and then checks his understanding.

references.title: Assessing fitness to drive: a guide for medical professionals
references.note: Driving rules after an implantable cardioverter defibrillator.
